# Migrate an existing plugin to the current template

This guide brings an existing `epi-{make}-{model}` repository, created from an earlier version of this template, up to date with the template's build automation:

* README badges kept in sync by the build
* README plugin documentation generated by an MSBuild task (`build/ReadmeDocs.cs`), replacing the `update-readme` CI workflow
* A Husky.Net commit-msg hook that enforces conventional commit messages
* Shared package properties in `src/Directory.Build.props`
* `.gitattributes`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitignore` and VS Code tasks

The guide targets the template's `main` branch as of PR #38 (`784667e`). The [README](README.md) explains how each of these works; this guide covers only how to adopt them.

> **New plugins:** a repository created from the template already has all of this. You can delete this file from it.

## Before you start

* The plugin must be a 4-Series-only, SDK-style project (`<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">`) in `src/`, one level below the repository root. The build targets look for `../README.md`, `../build/ReadmeBadges.cs` and `../build/ReadmeDocs.cs` relative to `src/`. If the repository still has a 3-Series project, remove it first (see the template's PR #33).
* You need the [.NET SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download) and Git. `nuget.exe` is no longer required.
* Work on a branch. Commit the migration with a non-releasing type such as `chore` or `build`, so it does not trigger a version bump.

```
git switch -c chore/template-update
```

## 1. Fetch the template

Plugin repositories are created from the template, so they share no history with it and `git merge` does not work. Add the template as a remote instead, and check out individual paths from it:

```
git remote add template https://github.com/PepperDash/EssentialsPluginTemplate.git
git fetch template main
```

To see what a file looks like in the template without changing your copy:

```
git show template/main:src/Directory.Build.props
```

## 2. Copy the files that are the same in every plugin

These files contain nothing plugin-specific. Copy them as-is:

```
git checkout template/main -- \
    build/ReadmeBadges.cs \
    build/ReadmeDocs.cs \
    src/Directory.Build.targets \
    .config/dotnet-tools.json \
    .husky \
    .github/skills/update-readme-docs \
    .gitattributes
```

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `build/ReadmeBadges.cs` | README badge synchronizer, compiled by the build |
| `build/ReadmeDocs.cs` | Plugin documentation generator, compiled by the build |
| `src/Directory.Build.targets` | CPLZ packaging, git hook install, README badge and docs targets |
| `.config/dotnet-tools.json` | Pins the Husky.Net tool |
| `.husky/` | Commit-msg hook and its linter |
| `.github/skills/update-readme-docs/` | Copilot skill that regenerates and reviews the plugin documentation |
| `.gitattributes` | Line-ending rules (LF in the repository, CRLF for `.sln`, LF for hooks) |

If your repository changed `src/Directory.Build.targets`, review `git diff --cached src/Directory.Build.targets` and add your changes back.

## 3. Merge the files that have plugin-specific content

Copying these would overwrite the plugin's own values, so merge them by hand.

### `src/Directory.Build.props`

Shared properties moved from the csproj into this file. Take the template's version and set the plugin's values:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <Version>1.0.0-local</Version>
    <InformationalVersion>$(Version)</InformationalVersion>
    <Authors>PepperDash Technology</Authors>
    <Company>PepperDash Technology</Company>
    <Product>PepperDash Essentials Plugin Samsung MDC</Product>
    <Copyright>Copyright © 2026</Copyright>
    <RepositoryUrl>https://github.com/PepperDash/epi-samsung-mdc.git</RepositoryUrl>
    <RepositoryType>git</RepositoryType>
    <PackageOutputPath>..\output</PackageOutputPath>
    <GeneratePackageOnBuild>True</GeneratePackageOnBuild>
    <PackageLicenseFile>LICENSE.md</PackageLicenseFile>
    <PackageReadmeFile>README.md</PackageReadmeFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <None Include="..\LICENSE.md" Pack="true" PackagePath=""/>
    <None Include="..\README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath=""/>
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
```

Keep any other properties your existing file already sets.

### The csproj

1. Remove the properties that are now in `Directory.Build.props`: `Version`, `InformationalVersion`, `Authors`, `Company`, `Copyright`, and any of the others listed above.
2. Remove any `None Include="..\README.md"` or `None Include="..\LICENSE.md"` items, which are now in `Directory.Build.props`. Duplicates cause packing errors.
3. Remove leftover items such as `<None Remove="../output\epi-....cplz" />`.
4. Keep `<ProjectType>ProgramLibrary</ProjectType>`. The README targets run only for that project type.
5. Keep the plugin's `AssemblyTitle`, `Description`, `PackageId`, `PackageProjectUrl`, `PackageTags` and `RootNamespace`.

Compare with the template's csproj: `git show template/main:src/epi-make-model.4Series.csproj`.

### `.gitignore`, `.editorconfig` and `.vscode/`

* `.gitignore`: the template's version is much shorter and ignores `output/`, `*.cplz` and `*.nupkg`. Replace yours with it, then add back any entries the plugin needs.
* `.editorconfig`: the template uses tabs for C# files. Take it if the plugin should follow the same style (see [Optional cleanup](#7-optional-cleanup)).
* `.vscode/tasks.json`: adds the "Install git hooks" task (runs on folder open) and "Update README docs". If you have no tasks of your own, check it out from the template; otherwise merge the three tasks into your file.
* `.vscode/settings.json` and `.vscode/extensions.json`: optional. The template no longer sets workspace colors.

## 4. Remove the README CI workflow

Delete the old README workflow:

```
git rm .github/workflows/essentialsplugins-updatereadme-caller.yml
```

That workflow runs `metadata.py` in CI and pushes its output. The build now generates the README itself, and its output differs from `metadata.py`. If you keep the workflow, the two overwrite each other and the release build fails with `PDREADME005`.

Keep `.github/workflows/EssentialsPlugins-builds-caller.yml`. It is unchanged.

## 5. Prepare the source and README

The README targets fail the build if these conditions are not met. Check them before the first build.

### Minimum Essentials version

At least one factory must set the minimum version in this form, on its own line:

```csharp
MinimumEssentialsFrameworkVersion = "2.42.4";
```

An expression-bodied property or an assignment that shares a line with other code is not recognized, and the build fails with `PDREADME001`.

The `PepperDashEssentials` `PackageReference` version in the csproj must be the same version or higher, or the build fails with `PDREADME002`. A prerelease of the minimum, such as `3.0.0-rc.11` for `3.0.0`, is allowed with a `PDREADME006` warning until the release is published.

### Type names

Write `TypeNames` with parentheses after `List<string>`:

```csharp
TypeNames = new List<string>() { "samsungMdc" };
```

Without the parentheses, the Supported Types section is still generated, but the Config Example `type` is not set.

### Badges

Add the two badges at the top of `README.md`, below the logo. The alt texts must be exactly `.NET` and `PepperDash Essentials`, or every build fails with `PDREADME003`. The values do not matter; the build corrects them.

```markdown
![PepperDash Essentials](https://img.shields.io/badge/PepperDash%20Essentials-≥%20v2.0.0-blue)
![.NET](https://img.shields.io/badge/.NET%20Framework-4.7.2-512BD4)
```

### Plugin documentation markers

READMEs generated by the old workflow already contain the `<!-- START name -->` / `<!-- END name -->` markers, and the new generator uses the same names. If a section's markers are missing, the generator appends the section at the end of the README. Move it to where you want it after the first run.

Sections you marked `<!-- SKIP -->` stay as they are, except the Config Example, which is now always regenerated. Set its values with `<example>` blocks on the config class's properties (see [Set the Config Example values](README.md#set-the-config-example-values)).

## 6. Build, generate and commit

1. Build. This restores the packages, installs the git hooks and updates the badges:

   ```
   dotnet build
   ```

2. Regenerate the plugin documentation and review it:

   ```
   dotnet msbuild -t:UpdateReadmeDocs
   git diff README.md
   ```

   Expect a diff even if the README was up to date before: the new generator orders and formats sections differently (see [The documentation generator](README.md#the-documentation-generator)). Fix any `SampleString`/`SampleValue` placeholders in the Config Example with `<example>` blocks and run the target again.

3. Commit:

   ```
   git add -A
   git commit -m "chore: adopt current plugin template build automation"
   ```

   The commit-msg hook checks this message. A message that does not follow the [commit message rules](README.md#commit-message-rules) is rejected.

GitHub Actions sets `CI=true`, so the release build checks the README instead of updating it. Commit the regenerated README before the next release, or the release build fails with `PDREADME004` or `PDREADME005`.

## 7. Optional cleanup

Make each of these a separate commit, so the migration commit stays easy to review.

* **Normalize line endings** after adding `.gitattributes`:

  ```
  git add --renormalize .
  git commit -m "chore: normalize line endings"
  ```

* **Reindent C# with tabs** to match `.editorconfig`: `dotnet format whitespace`, then commit with `style:`.
* **Delete leftovers from older templates**, if present: `GetPackages.BAT`, `.github/scripts/*.ps1`, an empty `.gitmodules`, and `src/Properties/` (`AssemblyInfo.cs` is replaced by `GenerateAssemblyInfo`; remove the `Properties\**` items from the csproj too).
* **Remove the template remote** when you are done: `git remote remove template`.

## 8. Verify

```
dotnet build
git config core.hooksPath
dotnet build -p:ReadmeMode=Check
```

* The first build succeeds and writes the `.cplz` and `.nupkg` to `output/`.
* `git config core.hooksPath` prints `.husky`.
* The check build succeeds, which is what the release build will do in CI.

Then push the branch and open a pull request.
